issue: Is a Rehaif error, where the court failed to advise the defendant that the government must prove knowledge of prohibited status under 18 U.S.C. § 922(g), a structural error that requires reversal without a showing of prejudice on plain-error review?

sides.position: The failure to instruct on or advise of the knowledge-of-status element is not a structural error; the defendant must show a reasonable probability he would have pleaded not guilty.
cases: United States v. Williams, 946 F.3d 968 (7th Cir. 2020)
United States v. Trujillo, 960 F.3d 1196 (10th Cir. 2020)
United States v. Tignor, No. 19-1158 (10th Cir. 2020)

sides.position: The failure to advise of the knowledge-of-status element is a structural error that requires reversal of the conviction without a showing of prejudice.
cases: United States v. Gary, 2020 WL 1443528 (4th Cir. Mar. 25, 2020)

this_court: not structural (sides with the Seventh Circuit and the Trujillo holding; the defendant must show a reasonable probability of a different plea outcome)
quote: Compare United States v. Williams, 946 F.3d 968, 972–73 (7th Cir. 2020) (concluding that this error was not structural), with United States v. Gary, ___ F.3d ___, 2020 WL 1443528, at *4 (4th Cir. Mar. 25, 2020) (concluding that this error was structural).
cite: United States v. Tignor, No. 19-1158 (10th Cir. 2020)
